title: Tuning Magnetic Properties Through Nanoparticle Shape Engineering and Assembly
summary: Our research explores how magnetic nanoparticles self-assemble into complex architectures, exhibiting emergent collective magnetic properties beyond individual particles. By controlling size, shape, and interparticle interactions, we create engineered assemblies—from 2D nanosheets to confined structures—with tailored magnetic anisotropy and enhanced heating efficiency for applications such as nanomedicine.
descriptionHtml: Our research explores how magnetic nanoparticles organize themselves into complex architectures and how this self-assembly unlocks emergent properties far beyond those of individual particles. By controlling size, shape, and interparticle interactions, we design assemblies with tailored magnetic anisotropy and collective relaxation dynamics, enabling precise modulation of heating efficiency and magnetic responsiveness. We focus on creating engineered architectures, from 2D magnetic nanosheets with enhanced multifunctionality to confined assemblies that retain their magnetic performance even in complex biological environments. This fundamental understanding of self-organization not only reveals how collective magnetic behavior arises but also provides a powerful design strategy for applications such as nanomedicine. Ultimately, our goal is to transform nanoparticle self-assembly into a predictive tool for building functional magnetic materials with tunable and programmable properties.
